title: KV beacon reservation and sparse prefill orchestrator
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Implement a 'decode beacon' driven reservation layer and a sparse-prefill orchestrator to improve paged-attention KV residency and reduce prefill / decode latency variance for long-context conversational workloads.

Motivation: Current paged-KV allocation and eviction policies oscillate under mixed short/long sessions, causing frequent slot thrashing and prefill stalls. Existing eviction heuristics (LRU + score-based compaction) do a good job on steady-state hotsets but fail to pre-warm or reserve capacity when a decode wave is predicted. This ticket designs a lightweight beacon signal emitted by the scheduler to reserve soft slots in targeted slabs, coordinate sparse prefill work, and introduce eviction hysteresis to reduce oscillation.

Goals:
- Add a per-shard "decode beacon" that carries a compact temporal fingerprint and target slot list so prefill workers can warm KV proactively.
- Implement soft reservation quotas (tiny token buckets per-tenant) that prevent aggressive eviction of reserved slots during prefill windows.
- Introduce a compactness fingerprint computed from access frequency + recent span to enable aliasing-resistant reuse decisions and avoid cross-tenant contamination.
- Build a sparse-prefill orchestrator that schedules background prefill tasks during low-GPU-util windows and throttles by kernel backpressure signals.
- Reduce 95th percentile prefill latency by ~15-25% and decrease KV miss rate for long-context sessions by ~20% in stanford-longchat-like workloads.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of slab allocator or global reclaim policy. We keep GC semantics identical; reservations are soft and degradable.

Trade-offs considered:
- Reservation size vs memory fragmentation: larger soft-reservations reduce prefill misses but increase fragmentation; we use small token counts (1-4 slots) per decode beacon to balance.
- Beacon frequency vs scheduler overhead: emitting beacons on every request increases control-plane cost; we anchor beacon emission to prefill/rollout triggers and large prefix hits.
- Background prefill vs latency interference: prefill runs must be gated by kernel queues and per-GPU SLOs to avoid hurting foreground decodes.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Asha K: Initial spike session with M. Ortega and E. Chen. We sketched the beacon wire-format: 64-bit time-since-last-touch + 16-bit compactness_hash + up to 8 (shard,slot_hint) pairs. Decided to avoid embedding tenant secrets in beacon payload.

2025-02-18 - Miguel O: Proof-of-concept ran on dev-cluster. Early results on Llama-2-Chat-13B long-context sim: 95p prefill latency down 18% (synthetic chat workload). Observable reduction in KV misses (~27%) for sessions >8k tokens when the beacon path is active.

2025-02-22 - Evelyn C (SRE): Concern about interaction with eviction throttles during out-of-memory spikes. Proposed eviction hysteresis window of 5s after a beacon reserve to prevent immediate reclaim.

2025-02-25 - Design review (Charlie M): Asked for schema-compatible fallback for older Dedicated nodes that don't support the beacon header. Decision: use opaque metadata mapped at shard-mgr; if unsupported, orchestrator falls back to opportunistic prefill only.
2025-02-27 - Miguel O: Microbenchmarks: background prefill consumes ~3-6% additional GPU cycles when gated properly; observed minimal impact on tail decode if gated behind kernel queue depth < 60%.
2025-03-03 - Asha K: Security review: no customer data written into beacons; compactness_hash is salted per-shard. Security team ok with 'low' risk; still flagged for review in Private deployments.
next_steps: 1) Merge schema + shard-mgr mapping PR and deploy canary to dedicated-dev cluster. 2) Implement soft-reservation accounting with eviction hysteresis and unit tests. 3) Add kernel queue gated prefill workers and end-to-end benchmark harness. 4) Run acceptance with runtime-1.21 canary and include Private deployment compatibility check.
acceptance_criteria:
- Beacon wire-format merged and shard-mgr mapping present.
- Soft reservation honors token counts and is degraded under memory pressure.
- Sparse-prefill orchestrator reduces 95p prefill latency by >=15% on long-context synthetic workload without increasing foreground decode 95p by >5%.
- No sensitive data transmitted in beacons and security review completed for hosted and private variants.
